arxiv-2110-08490.title: Collisions of the supercritical Keller-Segel particle system Thanks: The fruitful comments of the two referees helped us to substantially improve the presentation of the paper.
arxiv-2110-08490.creator: Nicolas Fournier and Yoan Tardy
arxiv-2110-08490.description: Abstract . We study a particle system naturally associated to the 2 2 -dimensional Keller-Segel equation. It consists of N N Brownian particles in the plane, interacting through a binary attraction in θ / ( N ​ r ) \theta/(Nr) , where r r stands for the distance between two particles.

arxiv-2110-09602.title: Biparametric persistence for smooth filtrations 0 0 footnotetext: The authors were supported by the ARO through the MURI ’Science of Embodied Innovation, Learning and Control’.
arxiv-2110-09602.creator: Mishal Assif P K, Yuliy Baryshnikov
arxiv-2110-09602.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Mishal Assif P K, Yuliy Baryshnikov. The goal of this note is to define biparametric persistence diagrams for smooth generic mappings h = ( f , g ) : M → V ≅ ℝ 2 h=(f,g):M\to V\cong\mathbb{R}^{2} for smooth compact manifold M M . Existing approaches to multivariate persistence are mostly centered on the workaround of absence of reasonable algebraic theories for quiver representations for lattices of rank 2 or higher, or similar artificial obstacles.

arxiv-2203-05344.title: EyeLoveGAN: Exploiting domain-shifts to boost network learning with cycleGANs
arxiv-2203-05344.creator: Josefine Vilsbøll Sundgaard, Kristine Aavild Juhl ⋆, Jakob Mølkjær Slipsager
arxiv-2203-05344.description: Abstract This paper presents our contribution to the REFUGE challenge 2020. The challenge consisted of three tasks based on a dataset of retinal images: Segmentation of optic disc and cup, classification of glaucoma, and localization of fovea. We propose employing convolutional neural networks for all three tasks.

arxiv-2204-06683.title: Revisiting Transformer-based Models for Long Document Classification
arxiv-2204-06683.creator: Xiang Dai, Ilias Chalkidis, Sune Darkner, Desmond Elliott
arxiv-2204-06683.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Xiang Dai, Ilias Chalkidis, Sune Darkner, Desmond Elliott. The recent literature in text classification is biased towards short text sequences (e.g., sentences or paragraphs). In real-world applications, multi-page multi-paragraph documents are common and they cannot be efficiently encoded by vanilla Transformer-based models. We compare different Transformer-based Long Document Classification (TrLDC) approaches that aim to mitigate the computational overhead of vanilla transformers to encode much longer text, namely sparse attention and hierarchical encoding methods.

arxiv-2304-13837.title: Low energy Eta-baryon interaction
arxiv-2304-13837.creator: M. G. L. Nogueira-Santos, C. C. Barros, Jr
arxiv-2304-13837.description: Abstract The η \eta -Baryon interactions at low energies are studied in a model based in effective chiral Lagragians that take into account baryons of spin 1/2 and spin 3/2 in the intermediate states. The interacting baryons to be considered in this work are B = N , Λ , Σ , Ξ B=N,\Lambda,\Sigma,\Xi .

arxiv-2304-14951.title: Excitons guided by polaritons
arxiv-2304-14951.creator: K. Mukherjee, S. Wüster
arxiv-2304-14951.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by K. Mukherjee, S. Wüster. We show that an exciton on a discrete chain of sites can be guided by effective measurements induced by an ambient, non-equilibrium medium that is synchronised to the exciton transport. For experimental verification, we propose a hybrid cold atom platform, carrying the exciton as electronic excitation on a chain of atoms, which are surrounded by a slow light medium supporting polaritons. The chain is coupled to the medium through long-range Rydberg interactions.

arxiv-2305-02023.title: The topology of poker Thanks: L.B. is partially supported by ERC AdG grant 101097307
arxiv-2305-02023.creator: Laurent Bartholdi, Roman Mikhailov
arxiv-2305-02023.description: Abstract . We examine the complexity of the “Texas Hold’em” variant of poker from a topological perspective. We show that there exists a natural simplicial complex governing the multi-way winning probabilities between various hands, and that this simplicial complex has dimension at least 4 4 .

arxiv-2308-02710.title: Evolutionary Multi-objective Optimisation in Neurotrajectory Prediction Journal: Journal of Applied Soft Computing
arxiv-2308-02710.creator: Edgar Galván (ORCID: 0000-0001-8474-5234), Fergal Stapleton (ORCID: 0000-0002-5347-1573)
arxiv-2308-02710.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Edgar Galván (ORCID: 0000-0001-8474-5234), Fergal Stapleton (ORCID: 0000-0002-5347-1573). Machine learning has rapidly evolved during the last decade, achieving expert human performance on notoriously challenging problems such as image classification. This success is partly due to the re-emergence of bio-inspired modern artificial neural networks (ANNs) along with the availability of computation power, vast labelled data and ingenious human-based expert knowledge as well as optimisation approaches that can find the correct configuration (and weights) for these networks.

arxiv-2403-17789.title: Molecular groundstate determination via short pulses on superconducting qubits
arxiv-2403-17789.creator: Noga Entin, Mor M. Roses, Reuven Cohen, Nadav Katz, Adi Makmal
arxiv-2403-17789.description: Abstract Quantum computing is currently hindered by hardware noise. We present a freestyle superconducting pulse optimization method, incorporating two-qubit channels, which enhances flexibility, execution speed, and noise resilience. A minimal 0.22 ns pulse is shown to determine the H 2 groundstate to within chemical accuracy upon real-hardware, approaching the quantum speed limit.

arxiv-2406-02782.title: KPZ scaling from the Krylov space
arxiv-2406-02782.creator: Alexander Gorsky 1,4 , Sergei Nechaev 2,4 , and Alexander Valov 3
arxiv-2406-02782.description: Abstract Recently, a superdiffusion exhibiting the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) scaling in late-time correlators and autocorrelators of certain interacting many-body systems, such as Heisenberg spin chains, has been reported. Inspired by these results, we explore the KPZ scaling in correlation functions using their realization in the Krylov operator basis.

arxiv-2411-01772.title: Joint optimization for production operations considering reworking
arxiv-2411-01772.creator: Yilan Shen, Boyang Li, Xi Zhang
arxiv-2411-01772.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yilan Shen, Boyang Li, Xi Zhang. In pursuit of enhancing the comprehensive efficiency of production systems, our study focused on the joint optimization problem of scheduling and machine maintenance in scenarios where product rework occurs. The primary challenge lies in the interdependence between product q uality, machine r eliability, and p roduction scheduling, compounded by the uncertainties from machine degradation and product quality, which is prevalent in sophisticated manufacturing systems.

arxiv-2506-08587.title: Chandra X-ray Measurement of Heavy Element Abundances of Wolf-Rayet Stars in the Galactic Center Chandra X-ray Measurement of Heavy Element Abundances of Wolf-Rayet Stars in the Galactic Center – 2
arxiv-2506-08587.creator: Ziqian Hua, Zhiyuan Li
arxiv-2506-08587.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ziqian Hua, Zhiyuan Li. Elemental abundances hold important information about the star formation history in the Galactic Center. The thermal X-ray spectra of certain stars can provide a robust probe of elemental abundances, mainly through the presence of K-shell emission lines.

arxiv-2511-07920.title: Lightweight Diffusion-based Framework for Online Imagined Speech Decoding in Aphasia Thanks: This work was partly supported by Institute of Information & Communications Technology Planning & Evaluation (IITP) grant funded by the Korea government (MSIT) (No. RS-2019-II190079, Artificial Intelligence
arxiv-2511-07920.creator: Eunyeong Ko, Soowon Kim, Ha-Na Jo
arxiv-2511-07920.description: Abstract A diffusion-based neural decoding framework optimized for real-time imagined speech classification in individuals with aphasia. The system integrates a lightweight conditional diffusion encoder and convolutional classifier trained using subject-specific EEG data acquired from a Korean-language paradigm. A dual-criterion early stopping strategy enabled rapid convergence under limited calibration data, while dropout regularization and grouped temporal convolutions ensured stable generalization.

arxiv-2512-18523.title: Two Photon Tripartite Entanglement Transfer via Time-Multiplexed Quantum Walks
arxiv-2512-18523.creator: Jonas Lammers, Federico Pegoraro, Philip Held, Nidhin Prasannan, Benjamin Brecht, Christine Silberhorn
arxiv-2512-18523.description: Abstract Photonic multidimensional quantum networks (MDQN), where individual subsystems are encoded using multiple degrees of freedom and photons, are an emerging platform for quantum algorithms because they offer high scalability. The distribution of non-classical and non-local correlations between the individual subsystems in an MDQN is of fundamental interest for many quantum protocols.

arxiv-2601-21186.title: From Logic to Toolchains: An Empirical Study of Bugs in the TypeScript Ecosystem Conference: 23rd International Conference on Mining Software Repositories; April 13–14, 2026; Rio de Janeiro, Brazil 23rd International Conference on Mining Software Repositories (MSR ’26), April 13–14, 2026, Rio de Jan
arxiv-2601-21186.creator: TianYi Tang, Saba Alimadadi, Nick Sumner
arxiv-2601-21186.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by TianYi Tang, Saba Alimadadi, Nick Sumner. TypeScript has rapidly become a popular language for modern web development, yet its effect on software faults remains poorly understood. This paper presents the first large-scale empirical study of bugs in real-world TypeScript projects. We analyze 633 bug reports from 16 popular open-source repositories to construct a taxonomy of fault types, quantify their prevalence, and relate them to project characteristics such as size, domain, and dependency composition.

europmc-pmc4209138.title: Orthology inference in nonmodel organisms using transcriptomes and low-coverage genomes: improving accuracy and matrix occupancy for phylogenomics.
europmc-pmc4209138.creator: Yang Y, Smith SA.
europmc-pmc4209138.description: Orthology inference is central to phylogenomic analyses. Phylogenomic data sets commonly include transcriptomes and low-coverage genomes that are incomplete and contain errors and isoforms. These properties can severely violate the underlying assumptions of orthology inference...

plos-pone-0000553.creator: Pearl A. Campbell, Carolina Perez-Iratxeta, Miguel A. Andrade-Navarro et al.
plos-pone-0000553.description: PLOS ONE research article. Stem cells are characterized by two defining features, the ability to self-renew and to differentiate into highly specialized cell types. The POU homeodomain transcription factor Oct4 ( Pou5f1 ) is an essential mediator of the embryonic stem cell state and has been implicated in

pmc-10716379.title: Microbial shifts associated to ENSO-derived thermal anomalies reveal coral acclimation at holobiont level
pmc-10716379.creator: Sandra Montaño-Salazar, Elena Quintanilla, Juan A Sánchez
pmc-10716379.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The coral microbiome conforms a proxy to study effects of changing environmental conditions. However, scarce information exists regarding microbiome dynamics and host acclimation in response to environmental changes associated to global-scale disturbances. We assessed El Niño Southern Oscillation (ENSO)-derived thermal anomalies shifts in the bacterial microbiome of Pacifigorgia cairnsi (Gorgoniidae: Octocorallia) from the remote island of Malpelo in the Tropical Eastern Pacific. Malpelo is a hot spot of biodiversity and lacks direct coastal anthropogenic impacts.

pmc-11455086.title: 5112 Late-Onset And Reversible Adrenal Insufficiency In Survivors Of Coronavirus Disease 2019: Results From A 24-Month Longitudinal Study
pmc-11455086.creator: Saroj Kumar Sahoo, Jayakrishnan C Menon, Subhash B Yadav
pmc-11455086.description: Disclosure: S.K. Sahoo: None. J.C. Menon: None. S.B. Yadav: None. Purpose We studied the temporal course of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) dysfunction in patients with corona-virus disease (COVID19). Methods Three-hundred and two patients (median age 54 years [interquartile range 42-64], 76% males, 97 with severe/critical illness) were recruited.

pmc-11487063.title: TRIM55 restricts the progression of hepatocellular carcinoma through ubiquitin-proteasome-mediated degradation of NF90
pmc-11487063.creator: Changhong Luo, Yuyan Lu, Qinliang Fang, Jing Lu, Ping Zhan, Wenqing Xi, Jinzhu Wang, Xijun Chen, Qin Yao, Fuqiang Wang, Zhenyu Yin, Chengrong Xie
pmc-11487063.description: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a prevalent malignant tumor worldwide. Tripartite motif containing 55 (TRIM55), also known as muscle-specific ring finger 2 (Murf2), belongs to the TRIM protein family and serves as an E3 ligase. Recently, the function and mechanism of TRIM55 in the advancement of solid tumors have been elucidated.

pmc-12595147.title: Association between maternal serum levels of Alpha-Fetoprotein and eruption timing of the first central deciduous tooth: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12595147.creator: Elham Faghihian, Shamin Ghobadi, Rasool Rezaei, Zahra Saberi
pmc-12595147.description: The current study investigated the relationship between the first central deciduous tooth eruption time and serum levels of maternal alpha-fetoprotein and related multiple of the median (MoM). The cross-sectional study was performed on a convenient sample of children aged 12 to 27 months in Isfahan City, Iran.

pmc-12634006.title: A Novel Eye Tracking–Based Gamified Assessment of Contrast Sensitivity Function in Children: Prospective Development and Reliability Study
pmc-12634006.creator: Yunsi He, Yijing Zhuang, Lei Feng, Xuanyu Xu, Ying Deng, Moruomi Li, Yangfei Pang, Ying Yao, Wentong Yu, Zixuan Xu, Yusong Zhou, Yudan Zhong, Qiuying Li, Qingqing Ye, Junpeng Yuan, Yun Wen, Jinrong Li
pmc-12634006.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundReliable assessment of visual function in young children remains a challenge. Contrast sensitivity function (CSF) is a sensitive and fundamental index of visual performance, yet existing pediatric CSF assessments lack objectivity and adaptability.

pmc-13002556.title: Qualitative Insights on Preventive Group Training in LTC Facilities: Key Influencing Factors
pmc-13002556.creator: Isabell Fesser, Klaus Hager, Simone Miller, Wenke Walther
pmc-13002556.description: BackgroundThe cluster randomised controlled trial OrkA (Orofaciopharyngeal and linguistic‐communicative activation in older age) aims to evaluate the efficacy of a preventive group programme for older adults in long‐term care (LTC) facilities. The programme objective is to support the maintenance of swallowing, speech and communication skills in later life.

pmc-13475125.title: General and disease-specific health literacy in patients with heart failure: an outcome analysis
pmc-13475125.creator: Klara Rebernik Grah, Mitja Lainscak, Jerneja Farkas
pmc-13475125.description: IntroductionLimited health literacy is common among patients with heart failure (HF), and the relative importance of general and disease-specific health literacy for patient outcomes remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate general and disease-specific health literacy in patients with HF and to examine their association with behavioural, patient-reported and clinical outcomes.

pmc-13644170.title: Spatiotemporal epidemiology of influenza in Fujian Province: an 18-year observational study
pmc-13644170.creator: Minhua Li, Shaojian Cai, Jiake Chen, Lu Qin, Meirong Zhan, Jinzhang Wang, Yu Jiang, Chuancheng Wu, Jianjun Xiang
pmc-13644170.description: ObjectiveTo investigate the spatiotemporal epidemiological characteristics and temporal trends of influenza in Fujian Province, China, from 2005 to 2022.MethodsDescriptive epidemiological methods were used to analyze the temporal, demographic, occupational, and regional distribution of influenza cases. Spatial autocorrelation analysis, trend surface analysis, and spatiotemporal scan statistics were applied to explore the spatial distribution and clustering characteristics of influenza.

pmc-13681568.title: A protective human antibody against respiratory syncytial virus by targeting a prefusion epitope across sites IV and V of the viral fusion glycoprotein
pmc-13681568.creator: Lianpan Dai, Jian Song, Lili Xu, Zhao Gao, Senyu Xu, Yan Chai, Liang Wang, Mi Yang, Tong Ma, Qihui Wang, Sushan Cao, Junming Yie, Gang Zou, Zhengde Xie, Jim Zhen Wu, George Fu Gao
pmc-13681568.description: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is one of the leading pathogens that cause lower respiratory tract infections in infants and the elderly. Passive immunoprophylaxis with monoclonal antibody (mAb) has been approved to prevent morbidity and mortality from RSV infection in infants.
